title: Triage runbook: snapshot linker and minimal-repro test builder
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Create a lightweight incident triage runbook and an automated pipeline that links an incident's telemetry (traces, request payload, model/config delta, infra variant) to a compact archival snapshot and produces a minimal reproducible test case for evals/regression suites.

Why: Recent incidents expose a high cost in manual reconstruction: engineers re-run large config diffs or search logs for hours. This work reduces mean-time-to-test by creating a deterministic shrinker that reliably finds a smallest failing input + exact environment signature (model hash, quantization profile, kernel selection hint, KV cache seed, sequence prefix).

Goals:
- Define an incident snapshot schema that captures: request id, truncated input context, tokenization artifacts, model version + weights hash, runtime config flags, node metadata, and relevant traces (span ids).
- Implement a "snapshot linker" service that, given an incident id or trace id, assembles the canonical artifact and uploads to storage with a reproducible path.
- Build a deterministic minimal-repro generator (shrinker) tuned for LLM behaviors (preserve prefixes that trigger cache/KV differences, maintain special tokens). Avoid naive random deletion; use heuristic-aware reduction (preserve structural tokens, named entities, sequence anchors).
- Auto-generate a small regression test that runs in the smoke-eval harness with golden-token assertions and a token-level divergence metric. Include KV/cache-specific toggles to reproduce stateful failures.

Success metrics: reduction in manual triage time by >=50% in first month, at least one production incident fully reconstructed end-to-end using the pipeline, and generated minimal tests flake <5% in CI for 7 days.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Initial spike: prototype snapshot schema + PoC linker. Found that some runtime kernel hints are populated only at startup; added requirement to persist kernel selection metadata in logs.
2026-03-04 - Design review with Runtime team (K. Morales): agreed to include quantization profile id and a short kernel fingerprint. Runtime team to provide accessor within 2 sprints.

2026-03-05 - Decision: use deterministic shrinker (heuristic guided) instead of randomized fuzzing to reduce CI flakiness. Trade-off: may miss non-monotonic failures; mitigation: run randomized fuzzer in nightly long tests.
2026-03-07 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/triage-snapshot/pull/42 implementing snapshot uploader + s3 pathing. Requesting review from infra and security for retention policy.

2026-03-08 - Security note from J. Rivera: retention config must honor dataset retention labels and redact PII from request payloads; added redaction step to pipeline (PII scrub regex + token-level mask).

2026-03-09 - Integration test: shrinker reduced a real incident from ~1.2k tokens to 28-token minimal repro while preserving failing token; initial repro run reproduced divergence in local smoke harness. Added generated test to local regressions/incident-99421.json.
2026-03-10 - Blocking: need a small runtime API to surface kernel fingerprint for archived runs (ENG-52041 referenced). Runtime API owned by Serving Runtime team; dependency ticket created.
2026-03-10 - Next steps: (1) complete security review for storage paths, (2) land PR for shrinker and linker, (3) add pipeline trigger from incident console UI and webhook for automatic generation.
notes: Implementation plan: 1) finalize schema and wire up to incident streamer, 2) implement linker microservice + storage contract, 3) integrate deterministic shrinker, 4) add CI job to run generated minimal tests in the smoke-eval harness, 5) monitor flakiness and iterate.

Operational considerations: snapshots are short-lived by default (30 days) with an opt-in archival for long-term use; sensitive payloads redacted. Cost estimate: ~0.5% storage increase for incidents at expected rate.
Open questions: how to represent 'approximate' kernel selection when binary differs between deployments; proposed approach: include kernel fingerprint + human-readable fallback note.
Rollback plan: generated tests are added behind a feature flag; if flakiness spikes, disable auto-run and keep archival for manual triage.
